St. Finnian of Moville

St. Finnian of Movilla · St. Finian of Moville · St. Findbarr of Movilla · Finnian

Introduction

St. Finnian of Moville was a monastic teacher and bishop of the Irish monastery at Movilla near Newtownards.

Read the published life [1]

Death / martyrdom

Death recorded in 579; cause not established in the cited material

Read circumstances and sources

Background

St. Finnian’s monastery was at Movilla near Newtownards in County Down. The name Moville in many English church sources refers to that foundation, rather than the modern town of Moville in Donegal. The historical reference records differing traditions about his family and possible British background.

[2] Scholarly historical biography · Opening identification and competing accounts of origin

Life and notable events

He was remembered for scriptural scholarship and the formation of monks. Early accounts associate him with the education of St. Columba of Iona; the OCA also names him as St. Comgall’s teacher. The historical reference distinguishes these early testimonies from a much later story about a copied Psalter and a battle.

[2] Scholarly historical biography · Early testimonies and later Psalter legend · [3] Ecclesiastical biography and commemoration · Opening paragraph naming Finnian and September 10

Death and historical limits

The cited reference places his death in 579. His surviving biographical material is uneven, and later traditions attach similar names to different foundations. This profile does not merge him automatically with Finnian of Clonard or supply an unsupported cause of death.

[2] Scholarly historical biography · Opening death date and discussion of the surviving Life

Commemoration and legacy

ROCOR’s official list names St. Finian, Abbot of Moville. The OCA’s life of his pupil gives his commemoration as September 10.

[1] Official diocesan recognition list · St Finian, Abbot of Moville · [3] Ecclesiastical biography and commemoration · Opening paragraph
